findings: The long low building and taller northern annex are separate survey bodies within the mapped cyclotron complex; treating them as one rectangular building would lose the raised/setback geometry.
The courtyard building has eight wall faces and a preserved roof opening. Its current public building name is unresolved; no 5203 identity is assumed.
Main cyclotron south face and courtyard outer faces show window groups and pale/light-blue framing, but source textures contain strong baked foliage and shadows.
Cyclotron main wall 3 has only 18.9% projected coverage and borders the taller annex; low coverage alone is not evidence that a blank replacement wall should be added there.
Annex projections are predominantly opaque pale surfaces; no reliable door/window layout is established. Its eight-face envelope can be reconstructed without inventing openings.
Native north-approach rays hit raw fragments instead of a clean annex envelope. A bounded cleanup must protect the adjoining cyclotron body and nearby MLZ building.

Visible vanilla dirt occurs in the preserved source world. Its authorship is not established; the current alignment code protects all ordinary blocks and edit records. Reconstruction must not erase it.
